topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture's place in the series and introduces its aims before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Mutation-driven clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic develops the evidence that mutations confer selective advantages through successive clonal expansion.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how altered transcriptional accessibility can drive tumor development without additional mutations.

topics.label: Cancer stem cells, tumor hierarchy and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how a cell's position in a differentiation hierarchy affects its capacity to initiate and sustain cancer.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness and cancer promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals enable mutation-bearing cells to acquire stemness and develop into tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive stromal cells as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

topics.label: Investigating cancer with single-cell and spatial omics
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how molecular profiling of human tissue can reveal tumor evolution and interactions within the microenvironment.

topics.label: Converging influences on cancer evolution and developmental susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains malignancy as the convergence of favorable evolutionary conditions and extends that synthesis to susceptibility during childhood development.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and identifies therapy as the subject of the next session.
